newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA LOTTERY BIDS SEEN ASSESSED BY MARCH '98.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA LOTTERY BIDS SEEN ASSESSED BY MARCH '98.

text.p: Bids by companies seeking to operate South Africa's planned national lottery should be evaluated by March next year, the state-appointed consultants said on Monday.

Pierre Trudeau of Deloitte and Touche told a parliamentary committee that quick action was needed by all parties involved if the lottery was to be in place by the end of 1998 -- a year later than originally planned.
"The target date that the evaluation committee has set is at the end of March... hopefully soon after that the lottery board will be in a position to appoint an operator," Trudeau said.
"We believe we have one chance in South Africa to establish a national lottery and we have to get it right the first time," he said.
Trudeau said enabling legislation needed to be finalised before parliament recessed in June, after which a lottery board could be established and a licensing agreement could be drafted.
The bidding process should close by the end of the year, he said.
